gaps.text: In-line measurement of Temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Start with one model per method as the baseline, then fuse the synchronised Raman and mid-IR blocks, scaled so that neither method dominates the joined model. The two probes must look at the same measurement point, and the two data streams must be normalised to a common time step before fusion, with each method keeping its own calibration and diagnostics. Keep the fused model only if it beats the best single method on held-out runs or batches.)

The supplied material gives no achievable accuracy, detection limit or response time for glucose or lactate measured in-line in cell-culture medium; those figures would have to come from the pilot itself.
No demonstrated in-line glucose or lactate result for a cell-culture process is supplied; the bioprocess section is a map of literature-reported accessible variables.

items.finding: The source notes that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For an in-line aqueous cell-culture measurement, this could inform the need to control or monitor temperature at the measurement point to reduce spectral variability.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The quote concerns NIR and MIR, not Raman, and comes from a review rather than a cell-culture study; it does not specify a temperature sensor or setpoint.

items.finding: The source describes high-level data fusion as working at the decision level, where supervised models are first fitted to each data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the proposed baseline of one model per method before fusing the Raman and mid-IR blocks.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general PAT data-fusion review and does not address cell-culture medium, Raman/mid-IR synchronisation, or scaling.

citation.quote: The high-level data fusion (HLDF) (also called "decision-level" fusion) works on a decision level. This means that the first step is to fit some supervised models to each data matrix.
citation.label: E01 ¶33

items.finding: The source states that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports checking whether the fused model adds value over the best single method and whether the methods are complementary rather than redundant.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general review and does not provide cell-culture-specific validation or fusion performance.
